steps.name: Read the instance format
steps.asked: Parse TSPLIB files: NODE_COORD_SECTION for coordinates and the lower-diagonal form for explicit distance matrices.

steps.name: Build the distance matrix
steps.asked: Turn an instance into the matrix every algorithm below consumes, so the solvers never touch the file format.

steps.name: Trivial method
steps.asked: Output the vertices in plain ascending index order as a placeholder tour, to prove the read-solve-write pipeline runs before any real algorithm exists.

steps.name: Held-Karp
steps.asked: The exact solver: dynamic programming over (vertex, subset) pairs, growing from single vertices to the full set to read off the optimal round trip.
steps.detail: Keep, for a fixed start and every subset of the other vertices, the length of the cheapest path that begins at the start, passes through exactly that subset, and finishes at one chosen vertex in it. Build these values up from one-vertex subsets to the complete vertex set, close the loop back to the start, and retrace which choice produced each value to recover the actual visiting order.

steps.name: A heuristic
steps.asked: An approximate method, for instances the exact one cannot reach.

steps.name: Performance evaluation
steps.asked: Execution time and tour length against instance size, on the provided TSPLIB benchmarks and on instances from instance_generator.py, written up with figures.
